stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group on the waiting list

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that held the pen between the teeth
The group that held the pen between the lips

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that studied in six short sessions
The group that studied in one long session

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They hypothesized that praise from the teacher would affect hand raising.

**Participants.** The sample was 50 second-grade students, recruited from one city. Parents gave informed consent, each child gave assent, and the plan was approved by an institutional review board. Families could withdraw at any time.

**Method.** The children were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

**Results.** The group that was praised: mean hand raises per week = 23. The group that received no special response: mean hand raises per week = 12. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Why do people sometimes fail to help in an emergency?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 80 students were randomly assigned to be alone or with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants who were alone reported the smoke after a mean of 58 seconds; those in groups took a mean of 196 seconds (p = 0.01), and many never reported it.

**Source B.** In interviews after a staged emergency, participants who had not helped often said that they 'assumed someone else had already called for help' or that 'nobody else looked worried, so it could not be serious.'

**Source C.** Researchers observed 300 staged incidents in which a person dropped a bag of shopping in the street. Help was offered in 82 percent of incidents on quiet streets and in 41 percent of incidents on crowded streets.

questions.stem: Avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive personality disorders belong to which cluster?

options.why: Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.
A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.
Correct. Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.
Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.

questions.explanation: Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.

questions.stem: An employee receives a paycheck every two weeks. Which schedule of reinforcement is this?

options.why: Correct. A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.
Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.
A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.
A variable-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses.

questions.explanation: A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.

questions.stem: Liam's hand jerks away from a hot stove before he feels any pain. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.
Motor neurons is the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.
Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.
Correct. The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.

questions.explanation: The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a taste aversion?

options.text: A learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness
options.why: Correct. This is what a taste aversion means.

options.text: The decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over
options.why: That describes habituation.

options.text: The inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others
options.why: That describes biological preparedness.

options.text: Learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli
options.why: That describes one-trial conditioning.

questions.explanation: A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the theory that we hear pitch because the rate of nerve impulses matches the frequency of the sound?

options.why: Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.
Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.
Sound localization is the ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears.
Correct. Frequency theory is the theory that we hear pitch because the rate of nerve impulses matches the frequency of the sound.

questions.explanation: Frequency theory is the theory that we hear pitch because the rate of nerve impulses matches the frequency of the sound.

questions.stem: Worried about a low grade, Deb meets her teacher, makes a study plan and joins a study group. Which kind of coping is this?

options.why: Correct. Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.
Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.
Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.

questions.explanation: Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.80. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow?

options.why: Free association is the psychodynamic technique in which the client says whatever comes to mind.
Hypnosis is a state of heightened suggestibility that can help reduce pain and anxiety but does not reliably recover memories.
Group therapy is the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support.
Correct. Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.

questions.explanation: Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes emerging adulthood?

options.text: The belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them
options.why: That describes the imaginary audience.

options.text: The period from about 18 to the mid-twenties, between adolescence and full independence
options.why: Correct. This is what emerging adulthood means.

options.text: The belief of adolescents that they are unique and that bad things will not happen to them
options.why: That describes the personal fable.

options.text: The play in which children act out imaginary roles and situations
options.why: That describes pretend play.

questions.explanation: Emerging adulthood is the period from about 18 to the mid-twenties, between adolescence and full independence.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a dendrite?

options.text: The long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells
options.why: That describes the axon.

options.text: The fatty layer around some axons that speeds up neural impulses
options.why: That describes the myelin sheath.

options.text: A branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons
options.why: Correct. This is what a dendrite means.

options.text: The endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters
options.why: That describes the axon terminals.

questions.explanation: A dendrite is a branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: A tourist calls another country's eating customs 'wrong' because they differ from the customs at home. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.
A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.
Correct. Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.

questions.explanation: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.

questions.stem: A doctor warns a pregnant patient that alcohol can cross the placenta and harm the developing baby. Alcohol is an example of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. A teratogen is a harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus.
Gross motor skills is the movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping.
The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.
Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.

questions.explanation: A teratogen is a harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect?

options.why: Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.
Falsifiability is the quality of a claim that it could be shown to be wrong by evidence.
A hypothesis is a testable prediction about the relationship between variables.
Correct. An experiment is the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect.

questions.explanation: An experiment is the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: A case study examines one individual in depth.
No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes reaction formation?

options.text: The defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness
options.why: That describes repression.

options.text: The defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses
options.why: Correct. This is what reaction formation means.

options.text: The defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities
options.why: That describes sublimation.

options.text: The defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development
options.why: That describes regression.

questions.explanation: Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white?

options.why: Correct. The opponent-process theory is the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white.
Dichromatism is a form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work.
Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.
Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.

questions.explanation: The opponent-process theory is the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white.

questions.stem: To open a combination lock, Wes tries 000, then 001, then 002, and so on until it opens. Which problem-solving strategy is he using?

options.why: Correct. An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.
Divergent thinking is thinking that produces many possible answers to a problem.
Executive functions is the mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior.
A heuristic is a simple thinking shortcut that is fast but can lead to errors.

questions.explanation: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the lobes at the top of the head, which process touch and spatial information?

options.why: The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.
The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.
The occipital lobes is the lobes at the back of the head, which process visual information.
Correct. The parietal lobes is the lobes at the top of the head, which process touch and spatial information.

questions.explanation: The parietal lobes is the lobes at the top of the head, which process touch and spatial information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age?

options.why: The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.
Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.
Scaffolding is the temporary support that a more skilled person gives a learner and gradually removes.
Correct. Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.

questions.explanation: Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.
Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: The smell of sunscreen instantly brings back a vivid memory of a childhood holiday. Which sense has this close link to emotion and memory areas?

options.why: Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.
Correct. Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.
A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.

questions.explanation: Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: The group that was promised a certificate
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: The group that drew without a reward
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: A survey asks people to rate their happiness and their satisfaction with life on a scale of 1 to 10. What is the survey measuring?

options.why: Resilience is the ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship.
Posttraumatic growth is the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event.
Gratitude is the appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being.
Correct. Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.

questions.explanation: Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.

questions.stem: In a group where everyone else gives an obviously wrong answer about the length of a line, a participant gives the same wrong answer. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.
Correct. Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.
Collectivism is the cultural pattern that gives priority to the goals of the group and defines identity by group membership.
Obedience is the following of the direct commands of an authority figure.

questions.explanation: Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The amount of caffeine consumed each day
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study?

options.why: Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.
Correct. Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.
Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.

questions.explanation: Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: The group asked the question with the word 'contacted'
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: The group asked the question with the word 'smashed'
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Positive psychologists group creativity, curiosity, judgment and love of learning under which virtue?

options.why: Humanity is the category of character strengths that includes love, kindness and social intelligence.
Correct. Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.
Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.
Temperance is the category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control.

questions.explanation: Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes denial?

options.text: The defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality
options.why: Correct. This is what denial means.

options.text: The defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior
options.why: That describes rationalization.

options.text: The defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people
options.why: That describes projection.

options.text: The defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one
options.why: That describes displacement.

questions.explanation: Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.

questions.stem: Receptor cells in the eye change light energy into neural signals the brain can use. What is this process called?

options.why: The absolute threshold is the weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time.
Sensory adaptation is the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation.
Correct. Transduction is the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses.
Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.

questions.explanation: Transduction is the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses.

questions.stem: After damage to a small structure below the thalamus, a rat stops eating and no longer regulates its body temperature. Which structure is damaged?

options.why: Correct. The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.
The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.
The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.

questions.explanation: The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.

questions.stem: In a famous drawing, people see either a white vase or two black faces, depending on which part they treat as the background. Which Gestalt principle explains this?

options.why: Correct. Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.
Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.
Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.
Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.

questions.explanation: Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.

questions.stem: A child with a mental age of 10 and a chronological age of 8 is given a score of 125. What is this score called?

options.why: Correct. The intelligence quotient is originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100.
Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.
The Flynn effect is the steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations.
General intelligence is the single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks.

questions.explanation: The intelligence quotient is originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100.

questions.stem: The highest score on a test is 98 and the lowest is 41, giving a value of 57. Which statistic is this?

options.why: Correct. The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.
A percentile rank is the percentage of scores in a distribution that fall at or below a given score.
The mode is the score that occurs most often.
The median is the middle score when the scores are placed in order.

questions.explanation: The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future?

options.why: A fixed mindset is the belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed.
An achievement test is a test that measures what a person has already learned.
Correct. An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.
Stereotype lift is the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped.

questions.explanation: An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a person's overall feeling of self-worth?

options.why: A personality inventory is a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits.
Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.
Self-concept is all the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'.
Correct. Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.explanation: Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm?

options.why: Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.
Correct. Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.
Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.

questions.explanation: Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress?

options.why: Correct. Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.
Leptin is the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger.
Melatonin is the hormone released by the pineal gland that makes a person sleepy.

questions.explanation: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.

questions.stem: Tia loves parties, talks easily to strangers and feels energized by being with people. She would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.
Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.
Correct. Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.
Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.

questions.explanation: Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict?

options.why: Correct. Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.
Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Standardization is the giving and scoring of a test in the same way for everyone, and the comparison of scores with a pretested group.
Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.

questions.explanation: Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: After losing a match, Eli thinks, 'I always fail at everything, and it is all my fault.' Which explanatory style is this?

options.why: The actor-observer bias is the tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits.
Correct. A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.
The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.
The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.

questions.explanation: A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Antidepressants, antipsychotics and mood stabilizers all belong to which general category of treatment?

options.why: Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.
Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient.
Correct. Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.
A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.

questions.explanation: Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.

questions.stem: To work out 23 × 4 in her head, Elif holds the numbers in mind and manipulates them. Which memory system is she using?

options.why: Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.
Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.
Correct. Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.
Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.

questions.explanation: Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.

questions.stem: The sudden appearance of a snake on the path triggers fear in a hiker. The snake is acting as which of the following?

options.why: The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.
Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.
Correct. An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.
A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.

questions.explanation: An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.

questions.stem: On the phone with her grandfather, a three-year-old nods silently in answer to his questions, assuming he can see her. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Conservation is the understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes.
Animism is the belief of young children that lifeless objects have feelings and intentions.
Theory of mind is the understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings.
Correct. Egocentrism is the difficulty that young children have in taking another person's point of view.

questions.explanation: Egocentrism is the difficulty that young children have in taking another person's point of view.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes integrity versus despair?

options.text: Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are
options.why: That describes identity versus role confusion.

options.text: Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret
options.why: Correct. This is what integrity versus despair means.

options.text: Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work
options.why: That describes generativity versus stagnation.

options.text: Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships
options.why: That describes intimacy versus isolation.

questions.explanation: Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the sudden realization of the solution to a problem?

options.why: Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.
Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.
A cognitive map is a mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings.
Correct. Insight learning is the sudden realization of the solution to a problem.

questions.explanation: Insight learning is the sudden realization of the solution to a problem.

questions.stem: Kai is consistently attracted to people of the same sex. Which term describes this pattern of attraction?

options.why: Correct. Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.
Gender identity is a person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination.
A gender role is the set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women.
Sex is the biological characteristics, such as chromosomes and anatomy, by which people are classified as male, female or intersex.

questions.explanation: Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.

questions.stem: Mr. Diaz snores loudly, stops breathing many times each night, and feels exhausted during the day. Which sleep disorder does he most likely have?

options.why: Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.
Correct. Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.
REM sleep behavior disorder is a sleep disorder in which the normal paralysis of REM sleep is missing, so the person acts out dreams.
Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.

questions.explanation: Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.

questions.stem: Red light and blue light differ in color. Which property of the light waves differs?

options.why: Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.
Correct. Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.
The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.
Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.

questions.explanation: Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the exosystem?

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child
options.why: That describes the macrosystem.

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace
options.why: Correct. This is what the exosystem means.

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school
options.why: That describes the microsystem.

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings
options.why: That describes the mesosystem.

questions.explanation: The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Although he is not hungry, Karl buys a cake because it looks and smells delicious. Which theory of motivation best explains this?

options.why: Self-determination theory is the theory that people are motivated by needs for competence, autonomy and relatedness, either from within or from outside.
Arousal theory is the theory that people are motivated to keep an ideal level of alertness and stimulation.
Homeostasis is the body's tendency to keep its internal state, such as temperature, steady.
Correct. Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.

questions.explanation: Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.

questions.stem: A therapist keeps every appointment, honors his commitments and protects the trust his clients place in him. Which ethical principle is he following?

options.why: Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.
Correct. Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.
Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.

questions.explanation: Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.

questions.stem: A doctor prescribes a fast-acting drug that calms a patient's panic by slowing central nervous system activity, warning that it can cause dependence. Which kind of drug is this?

options.why: An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.
Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.
Correct. An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.
Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.

questions.explanation: An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.

questions.stem: After being bitten by a large brown dog, Eva is afraid of all dogs. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.
Acquisition is in classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned.
Stimulus discrimination is the learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli.
Correct. Stimulus generalization is the tendency to respond to stimuli that are similar to the conditioned stimulus.

questions.explanation: Stimulus generalization is the tendency to respond to stimuli that are similar to the conditioned stimulus.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered?

options.why: Posttraumatic stress disorder is the disorder in which a person has flashbacks, nightmares, watchfulness and avoidance for more than a month after a terrifying event.
Correct. Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.
Dissociative identity disorder is the disorder in which a person shows two or more distinct personalities that take control at different times.
An obsession is an unwanted thought or urge that keeps returning and causes anxiety.

questions.explanation: Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others?

options.why: Correct. Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.
Dependent personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior.
Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.
Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.

questions.explanation: Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Experiments also use numerical data.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Experiments also test hypotheses.
Sample size does not determine the research method.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Wearing masks in a large, excited crowd, normally law-abiding fans begin smashing windows. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Correct. Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.
Group polarization is the strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them.
Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.

questions.explanation: Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes effect size?

options.text: The measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is
options.why: Correct. This is what effect size means.

options.text: A procedure in which the participants do not know which condition they are in
options.why: That describes a single-blind procedure.

options.text: An improvement that results from a person's expectation of a treatment rather than from the treatment itself
options.why: That describes the placebo effect.

options.text: A factor other than the independent variable that differs between groups and could explain the results
options.why: That describes a confounding variable.

questions.explanation: Effect size is the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is.

questions.stem: A psychologist says a client's anxiety comes from unresolved childhood conflicts that the client is not aware of. Which perspective is this?

options.why: The evolutionary perspective is the view that disorders involve behaviors that once helped survival but are now harmful.
The humanistic perspective is the view that disorders result from blocked personal growth and a lack of acceptance.
Correct. The psychodynamic perspective is the view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood.
The sociocultural perspective is the view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination.

questions.explanation: The psychodynamic perspective is the view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood.

questions.stem: According to Freud, a person may be unable to recall a painful childhood event because the mind has blocked it from consciousness. What did Freud call this?

options.why: Correct. Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.
Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.
The forgetting curve is the pattern in which memory fades quickly at first and then levels off.
Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.

questions.explanation: Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.

questions.stem: A dentist's drill causes pain, and soon the sound of the drill alone makes Ben tense. In this example, the sound of the drill is which of the following?

options.why: The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.
Correct. The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.
The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.

questions.explanation: The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.

questions.stem: To learn forty new vocabulary words, Felix must concentrate and rehearse them. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Explicit memory is the memory of facts and experiences that a person can consciously recall and state.
Semantic encoding is the deep encoding of a word based on its meaning.
Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.
Correct. Effortful processing is the encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.

questions.explanation: Effortful processing is the encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to favor the members of one's own group?

options.why: Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.
Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.
Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.
Correct. In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.

questions.explanation: In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.

questions.stem: A baseball player wore odd socks on the day he hit three home runs, and he has worn odd socks at every game since. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.
A primary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as food or water, that satisfies a biological need and is rewarding without learning.
Shaping is the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior.
Correct. Superstitious behavior is a behavior that is repeated because it happened by chance just before a reward.

questions.explanation: Superstitious behavior is a behavior that is repeated because it happened by chance just before a reward.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 500 and a standard deviation of 20. About what percentage of scores are between 480 and 520?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. About 68% of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: About 68% of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean. (480 and 520 are one standard deviation from the mean; 460 and 540 are two.)

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the children to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of hand raising

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of hand raising.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Hand raising was defined as the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The praised group raised their hands more often. On average, the value was 23 for the group that was praised and 12 for the group that received no special response, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent and assent: parents consented and each child agreed to take part. (Also acceptable: approval by an institutional review board; the right to withdraw.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 50 second-grade students from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The praised group raised their hands more often. (23 compared with 12).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that praise from the teacher affects hand raising. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to praise from the teacher. The finding illustrates positive reinforcement: adding a pleasant consequence after a behavior makes the behavior more frequent.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Why do people sometimes fail to help in an emergency?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: People are less likely to help when others are present, because each person feels less responsible and looks to others to decide how to act.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, participants who were alone reported smoke after 58 seconds, but those in groups of five took 196 seconds.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility: when others are present, each person feels less personal responsibility to act.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants said that 'nobody else looked worried, so it could not be serious.'

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through informational social influence: in an unclear situation, people use the behavior of others as evidence of what is happening, so if nobody reacts, each person concludes there is no emergency.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
